name: Roman Polanski
milestone_by_age_26: His student short film 'Two Men and a Wardrobe' (1958) won awards at multiple international film festivals including Brussels, San Francisco, and Oberhausen while he was at the Łódź Film School, and he graduated with a diploma in 1959.
early_history_summary: Polanski survived the Holocaust as a child in Krakow, began acting in radio and theatre as a teenager, and appeared in Andrzej Wajda's film 'A Generation' (1955) before entering the Łódź Film School. His student shorts from 1957-1959 already garnered international festival recognition, establishing him as a distinctive filmmaker before his first feature at age 29.
family_context_summary: Born in Paris to Polish-Jewish parents; mother died in Auschwitz. Survived the Holocaust wandering the Polish countryside. Father survived and reunited with him in 1945. No financial platform documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Parents were not in the film industry.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Łódź Film School, Holocaust survival, early acting, award-winning shorts
evidence_summary: Polanski's early career was shaped by extreme adversity during the Holocaust, which forced independence from a young age. He gained entry to the elite Łódź Film School, which provided access to film equipment and a network of future filmmakers. His student shorts won international festival awards before age 26, demonstrating exceptional technical depth and concentration. No family financial or domain advantages are documented; his trajectory was largely self-created through the institutional pipeline of the Polish film school system.

name: Lys Assia
milestone_by_age_26: Achieved a major hit recording with 'O mein Papa' in 1950 at age 26, having already built an established recording and performing career since her first contract with His Master's Voice in 1942.
early_history_summary: Born Rosa Mina Schärer in Rupperswil, Switzerland, she took classical ballet lessons as a child and debuted as a dancer at 16 at the Corso Theatre in Zurich. She switched to singing during WWII, entertaining troops in France, and secured her first recording contract with His Master's Voice in 1942. By 1950 she had breakthrough hits and toured the US.
family_context_summary: Born the youngest of 12 siblings in Rupperswil, Aargau, Switzerland. Family financial circumstances not documented in detail. She earned her own money from age 14.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parents in music or entertainment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early performing, recording contract, radio exposure, European touring
evidence_summary: Assia built her career through early and sustained performing, starting as a dancer at 16 and transitioning to singing during WWII. She secured a recording contract by 1942 (age 18) and achieved breakthrough hits by 1950 (age 26). Her path was largely self-created through direct domain exposure — performing for troops, at theatres, and on radio. No family domain or financial advantages are documented. She later won the first Eurovision Song Contest in 1956 at age 32, but her material milestone of hit recordings and an established career came by 26.

name: Bryan Adams
milestone_by_age_26: Released his debut album on A&M Records at age 20 (1980), and by 25 his album 'Reckless' (1984) reached #1 in the US and Canada, became the first Canadian album certified diamond, and produced multiple top-ten hits including the US #1 single 'Heaven'.
early_history_summary: Adams grew up in a diplomatic family, living in England, Israel, Portugal, and Austria before settling in Vancouver. He left school to pursue music, became lead vocalist of Sweeney Todd at 15, and began a crucial songwriting partnership with Jim Vallance at 18. A&M Records signed him as a recording artist, and his debut album was released at 20.
family_context_summary: Son of a British Army officer turned Canadian foreign service diplomat and UN peacekeeping observer. Family moved frequently. Adams used funds his parents saved for his college education to buy a piano. Modest financial circumstances during early career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Father was a military officer and diplomat, not in the music industry.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early band, Jim Vallance partnership, A&M Records, Vancouver music scene, MTV era
evidence_summary: Adams pursued music with single-minded focus from his mid-teens, leaving school and working as a session vocalist and dishwasher to fund his career. The songwriting partnership with Jim Vallance (former Prism member) was a critical complementary relationship that produced his biggest hits. A&M Records signed the pair as songwriters before signing Adams as an artist. His trajectory benefited from the MTV-era rock boom and direct immersion in the Vancouver music scene. Family provided modest support (college fund redirected to music) but no domain-specific advantages.

name: Rihanna
milestone_by_age_26: Her debut single 'Pon de Replay' reached #2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2005 at age 17, and her debut album 'Music of the Sun' was released the same year on Def Jam Recordings.
early_history_summary: Born in Saint Michael, Barbados, Rihanna grew up singing in her bedroom and won a high school talent contest. At 15, she was discovered by American producer Evan Rogers during his vacation in Barbados. Rogers arranged for her to record a demo in New York, which led to an audition with Jay-Z at Def Jam, where she was signed on the spot at age 16.
family_context_summary: Born to Ronald Fenty (warehouse supervisor) and Monica Fenty (accountant) in Barbados. Grew up in a modest three-bedroom bungalow. Mother ran a reggae club. Parents divorced when she was 14. No financial platform or inherited business network documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother ran a reggae club, providing early exposure to music. No professional music industry connections in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Evan Rogers discovery, Def Jam, Jay-Z, Caribbean music background, talent show
evidence_summary: Rihanna's breakthrough was catalyzed by the mentorship and industry connections of producer Evan Rogers, who discovered her at 15 in Barbados and arranged her demo and label audition. Jay-Z signed her to Def Jam on the spot at 16. Her Caribbean background and mother's reggae club provided early musical exposure, but she had minimal formal training. The Def Jam pipeline and the Caribbean-to-US music crossover wave were key structural advantages. Her vocal talent was evident but her early success was driven more by distribution and network than by deep skill or extensive prior reps.

name: Satyajit Ray
milestone_by_age_26: Fame arrived at age 34 with Pather Panchali (1955); by age 26 he was working as a commercial artist and had co-founded the Calcutta Film Society in 1947, but no material filmmaking milestone occurred by 26.
early_history_summary: Ray was born into a distinguished Bengali literary family in Calcutta. He studied economics at Presidency College and art at Visva-Bharati University before working as a commercial artist from 1943. He founded the Calcutta Film Society in 1947 and met Jean Renoir in 1949, but did not begin filmmaking until the early 1950s.
family_context_summary: Born into a prominent Bengali intellectual family. Father Sukumar Ray was a noted poet and writer; grandfather Upendrakishore Ray Chowdhury was a well-known litterateur, painter, and photographer. Father died when Satyajit was two and a half.
evidence_summary: Ray came from a distinguished literary and artistic family but did not begin his filmmaking career until his 30s. By age 26 he was a commercial artist who had co-founded a film society — a meaningful cultural activity but not a material career milestone in filmmaking. His first film, Pather Panchali, was released in 1955 when he was 34.

name: Cesare Maldini
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Serie A title (Scudetto) with AC Milan in his first season 1954-55 at age 22-23, and won a second Scudetto in 1956-57 at age 24-25, as a starting defender.
early_history_summary: Born in Trieste to a sailor father, Maldini grew up in the Servola neighborhood and developed a passion for football in the local oratory. He joined Triestina's youth system and debuted in Serie A in 1953 at age 21. He transferred to AC Milan in 1954 and immediately became a starter, winning the Scudetto in his first season.
family_context_summary: Son of Albino Maldini, a sailor, and Maria Vodeb. Family was of Slovenian descent from Trieste. No financial or football-specific family advantages documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Father was a sailor, not in football.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Triestina youth, AC Milan, Serie A, Nereo Rocco
evidence_summary: Maldini's path to early success ran through the Italian football performance pipeline: Triestina's youth academy to AC Milan at 22. He won the Scudetto in his first season at Milan (1954-55) and again in 1956-57, both before age 26. The elite ecosystem of Serie A and AC Milan's strong squad (with stars like Gunnar Nordahl and Nils Liedholm) provided a high-performance environment. No family domain or financial advantages are documented; his trajectory was driven by the institutional pipeline and his own athletic ability.

name: Christiane Nüsslein-Volhard
milestone_by_age_26: Nobel-winning research came in the 1980s-1990s; by age 26 she had completed a biochemistry diploma (1968) but had no material research milestone. Her PhD was completed in 1973-74 at age 31.
early_history_summary: Born in Magdeburg, Germany, Nüsslein-Volhard developed an interest in biology by age 12. She studied at Goethe University Frankfurt and then the University of Tübingen, completing her diploma in biochemistry in 1968. She began her PhD at the Max Planck Institute for Virus Research in 1969, working on protein-DNA interactions.
family_context_summary: Father was an architect, mother an artist and musician. Parents supported her interests with books. Middle-class family with five children. No scientific family domain documented, though her nephew Benjamin List also became a Nobel laureate.
evidence_summary: Nüsslein-Volhard completed her biochemistry diploma at age 26 but had not yet produced any material research milestone. Her PhD was completed at 31, and her Nobel-winning work on genetic control of embryonic development came in the 1980s. Her early path was characterized by university education without notable early research output.

name: Montserrat Caballé
milestone_by_age_26: Made her professional opera debut in 1956 at age 23 as Mimì in Puccini's La bohème at the Basel Opera, and sang multiple leading roles there through 1959, establishing a professional opera career by age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Barcelona to a humble family affected by the Spanish Civil War, Caballé entered the Liceu Conservatory at age 8 and studied singing with noted teachers including Napoleone Annovazzi, Eugenia Kemény, and Conchita Badía. She graduated with a gold medal in 1954, then moved to Basel where she made her professional debut as a last-minute replacement.
family_context_summary: Family was of humble financial circumstances due to the Spanish Civil War. Named after the Catalan monastery of Montserrat. Parents feared losing her and vowed to name her after the monastery if she survived.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parents in music or opera.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Liceu Conservatory, gold medal, Basel Opera, vocal training, humble origins
evidence_summary: Caballé's early career was built on intensive vocal training from age 8 at the Liceu Conservatory, where she won a gold medal in 1954. Multiple named teachers provided sustained, high-quality instruction. Despite humble family circumstances, the conservatory pipeline led directly to a professional opera career at Basel Opera by 23. She sang an astonishing range of roles in German and Italian opera during her Basel years (1957-1959). Her international breakthrough came later in 1965 at Carnegie Hall, but her professional opera career was firmly established by 26.

name: Zhang Yimou
milestone_by_age_26: Film career started at age 32; by age 26 he was working in a cotton textile mill during the Cultural Revolution with no material filmmaking milestone. He entered the Beijing Film Academy at age 28.
early_history_summary: Born in Xi'an to a family with Nationalist Army ties, Zhang faced political difficulties during the Cultural Revolution. He worked as a farm laborer for 3 years and then at a cotton textile mill for 7 years. He taught himself photography and sold his blood to buy his first camera. He entered the Beijing Film Academy's cinematography program in 1978 at age 28 after appealing an age-based rejection.
family_context_summary: Father was a dermatologist and former National Revolutionary Army officer; mother was a doctor. Family ties to the Nationalist movement caused political difficulties during the Cultural Revolution, severely limiting educational and career opportunities.
evidence_summary: Zhang's early life was defined by the Cultural Revolution, which interrupted his education and sent him to farm and factory work for a decade. He had no access to filmmaking until age 28, when he entered the Beijing Film Academy. His directorial debut, Red Sorghum, came at age 38. No material milestone in filmmaking occurred by age 26.

name: Vladimir Vysotsky
milestone_by_age_26: Graduated from the Moscow Art Theatre School in 1960 at age 22 and became a professional actor at the Moscow Pushkin Dramatic Theatre, then the Theatre of Miniatures, before joining the Taganka Theatre around 1964 at age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Moscow to a military communications officer father and a German translator mother, Vysotsky's parents divorced shortly after his birth. He developed an interest in theatre as a teenager, attended drama courses from 1953, and enrolled in the Moscow Art Theatre School in 1956 after briefly studying civil engineering. He began writing songs and performing with a guitar in the early 1960s.
family_context_summary: Father was a Jewish military communications officer and WWII veteran; mother was a German translator. Parents divorced shortly after his birth. He lived with his father and stepmother in Soviet-occupied Germany for two years as a child.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Parents were not in the performing arts.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Moscow Art Theatre School, Pushkin Theatre, Taganka Theatre, early songwriting, Bolshoy Karetny circle
evidence_summary: Vysotsky's early career was anchored in the elite Moscow Art Theatre School, which he entered at 18 after dropping out of engineering school. He became a professional actor at major Moscow theatres by 22 and joined the influential Taganka Theatre around 26. His songwriting began in the early 1960s within an informal circle of artists at Bolshoy Karetny Lane. No family domain or financial advantages are documented; his path was driven by the institutional theatre pipeline and his own intense focus. His immense cultural fame came after 26, but professional acting status was achieved by 22.

name: Jim Peebles
milestone_by_age_26: Nobel-winning cosmology research came in the 1960s-1970s; by age 26 he was a graduate student at Princeton, having received his bachelor's degree from the University of Manitoba. His PhD was completed in 1962 at age 27.
early_history_summary: Born in St. Boniface, Manitoba, Canada, Peebles was a self-described dreamer who studied engineering before switching to physics at the University of Manitoba. He entered Princeton University as a graduate student in 1958, where he studied under Robert Dicke and eventually became a pioneer of physical cosmology.
family_context_summary: Father worked as a clerk at the Winnipeg Grain Exchange. Peebles described himself as a dreamer and not a serious student in high school. No scientific family domain documented.
evidence_summary: Peebles was a graduate student at Princeton by age 26, having switched from engineering to physics during his undergraduate years. His Nobel Prize-winning contributions to physical cosmology came in the 1960s and 1970s, well after age 26. No material research milestone occurred by 26.

name: André Rieu
milestone_by_age_26: Founded his first orchestra (Maastricht Salon Orchestra) around 1978 at age 29; by age 26 he was still a conservatory student in Brussels. No material career milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Maastricht, Netherlands, Rieu was the son of a symphony orchestra conductor. He began violin lessons at age 5 and studied at conservatories in Liège, Maastricht, and Brussels, completing his training with the Premier Prix from the Royal Conservatory of Brussels in 1977. He then worked as a violinist in the Limburg Symphony Orchestra before founding his own ensemble.
family_context_summary: Father was conductor of the Maastricht Symphony Orchestra. Grew up in a household exclusively devoted to classical music. Third of six children, all of whom received musical training. This is a strong family-domain advantage.
evidence_summary: Rieu grew up in a strong musical family — his father was a symphony conductor — and studied violin from age 5 through multiple conservatories. However, despite this family-domain advantage and extensive training, he did not achieve a material career milestone by 26. He was still completing conservatory studies and had not yet founded his own orchestra or achieved notable recognition. His breakthrough came with the Johann Strauss Orchestra in 1987 at age 38.
